closest_prior_art_with_nontrivial_d2t_ca.category_name: Test Cover (minimum test set for exact identification)
closest_prior_art_with_nontrivial_d2t_ca.d2t_capability_gap: Test Cover is a deterministic binary covering problem (exact identification, no probabilities, no risk endpoint). D2T replaces this with probabilistic multi-action allocation under a randomised-minimax risk endpoint and a cost budget, with exact rational certificates -- a nontrivial extension beyond binary covering.

key_references: Chernoff 1959, Ann. Math. Statist. 30(3):345-360 (sequential design of experiments; delta^A) -- fixed-sample open-loop control is the special case

Nitinawarat, Atia & Veeravalli 2013, IEEE TAC 58(10):2451-2464 (controlled sensing for multihypothesis testing; fixed-sample open-loop is asymptotically optimal for binary HT; pure stationary open-loop policy)
categories.hypothesis_space: M-ary simple hypotheses (binary in Chernoff core); fully specified laws under each hypothesis
categories.action_control_space: Finite set of repeatable sensing actions/experiments; open-loop (pre-planned) integer allocation of samples to actions
categories.observation_model: Each action induces a categorical/multinomial observation law; conditionally independent given the chosen control
categories.fixed_sequential: Fixed sample size (fixed-sample open-loop); sequential variant exists (Chernoff sequential design) but the open-loop case is fixed-sample
categories.adaptive_nonadaptive: Non-adaptive (open-loop) for the fixed-sample case; adaptive for the sequential variant
categories.budget_cost: Sampling cost / fixed total sample size; per-action non-uniform costs in the 2013 extension
categories.loss_endpoint: Maximal error probability driven to zero asymptotically (error exponent / Chernoff information); decision-making risk in the sequential variant
categories.robustness_nuisance: None -- laws fully specified; technical 'positivity' assumption in Chernoff
categories.certificate_capability: Asymptotic (exponent) optimality only; no finite-budget exact risk certificate in the classical work
categories.computational_guarantee: Polynomial per-step allocation; asymptotic exponent-optimality; no exact finite-horizon guarantee
categories.rna_action_realism: N/A (generic sensing; no RNA action model)
categories.reduction_reasoning: The repo already runs a `chernoff` comparator (Chernoff-information greedy allocator, see evaluation/matrix.py), which is the frozen strongest comparator in track_c_primary_decision.json (coverage 60/64, family_cluster_mean_cost 8.0). This is a faithful instance of fixed-sample controlled sensing under the SAME task / information / cost / horizon / endpoint as D2T.
categories.d2t_capability_gap: GENUINE CLOSEST PRIOR ART. Nontrivial D2T capability left open: exact, finite-budget, interval-arithmetic-verified achievability upper bound and no-go lower bound for Track-C cost-to-fixed-risk-endpoint minimization, plus explicit oracle cross-validation -- none of which appear in the asymptotic (exponent-based) controlled-sensing literature (Chernoff delta^A is asymptotic and not second-order efficient; Keener 1984).

key_references: Naghshvar & Javidi 2013, Ann. Statist. 41(6):2703-2738 (active sequential hypothesis testing; dynamic-programming lower bounds; fixed-horizon is the non-stopping specialisation)
Naghshvar et al. 'Fixed-Horizon Active Hypothesis Testing and Anomaly Detection', IEEE TSP (adaptive allocation over a fixed horizon)
categories.hypothesis_space: M-ary simple hypotheses, Bayesian prior over hypotheses
categories.action_control_space: Finite set K of sensing actions; adaptive within a fixed horizon (or open-loop when adaptivity is disallowed)
categories.observation_model: Categorical observation laws per action, conditionally independent given action; Bayesian belief state update
categories.fixed_sequential: Fixed horizon (bounded number of observations); no early-stopping in the fixed-horizon form
categories.adaptive_nonadaptive: Adaptive (feedback) within the horizon in the active form; the repo comparator base is open-loop fixed-budget
categories.budget_cost: Fixed total cost / horizon length; sampling cost per action
categories.loss_endpoint: Error probability (or risk) minimised for a fixed horizon; DP lower bounds on optimal total cost
categories.certificate_capability: Dynamic-programming lower bounds and asymptotic optimality; no exact finite-budget rational certificate for the randomised-minimax endpoint
categories.computational_guarantee: DP is exponential in state for M>2; heuristic policies give asymptotic optimality; no poly exact solver for the cost-to-endpoint problem
categories.reduction_reasoning: A fixed-horizon, non-adaptive allocation is the SAME framework as the D2T fixed-budget-to-fixed-endpoint problem (allocation vector over a finite action set, bounded total cost, minimising risk). The repo comparators (full_matrix, random, chernoff, eig) are all fixed-budget open-loop allocations of this type and are run on the identical task.
categories.d2t_capability_gap: Leaves the same nontrivial D2T capability open as #1: exact certified finite-budget randomised-minimax and a certified no-go lower bound, rather than asymptotic exponents or unverified DP bounds.

key_references: Chernoff 1959 (sequential design, delta^A randomized policy)
Naghshvar & Javidi 2013, Ann. Statist. 41(6):2703-2738
Bessler 1960 (general M-ary sequential design)
categories.action_control_space: Finite set K of sensing actions chosen adaptively at each time step; stopping rule included
categories.observation_model: Categorical per-action laws; sequential belief update
categories.fixed_sequential: Sequential (variable-length): stopping time is part of the policy
categories.budget_cost: Total cost = cumulative control cost up to the stopping time; non-uniform control cost
categories.loss_endpoint: Expected total cost (delay + wrong-declaration penalty); asymptotic optimality in the Chernoff sense
categories.certificate_capability: Lower bounds via DP and asymptotic optimality; no exact finite-budget rational endpoint certificate
categories.computational_guarantee: Asymptotic optimality / positive information acquisition rate; DP exponential
categories.reduction_reasoning: The stopping-time (sequential) structure uses a genuinely different information/cost model than D2T: D2T Track C fixes the budget and minimises cost to a fixed risk endpoint with an integer open-loop allocation; active sequential HT adaptively stops. It is therefore COMPARABLE only on a SEPARATE track, not the same task/horizon/endpoint.
categories.d2t_capability_gap: Not the primary comparator track; a valid separate-track comparison would require its own pre-registered endpoint, not the frozen Track C endpoint.

categories.category_name: Robust T / KL discrimination (Huber, Wasserstein/TV uncertainty sets)
key_references: Huber 1965 (epsilon-contamination robust testing; least favourable distributions)
Chen, Gao & Ren 2015/2021 (general decision theory for Huber epsilon-contamination; robust minimax)
Wasserstein-uncertainty robust HT (DRO reformulations)
categories.hypothesis_space: Composite hypothesis classes / uncertainty sets around nominal laws (epsilon-contamination, TV/Wasserstein/KL balls)
categories.action_control_space: No action control in the classical framework (passive single observation stream); no multi-action allocation
categories.observation_model: Observation law lies in an uncertainty/contamination neighbourhood; minimax over the set
categories.fixed_sequential: Mostly fixed-sample; sequential e-value variants exist
categories.budget_cost: Sample complexity to bound worst-case error; no action-cost allocation
categories.loss_endpoint: Worst-case (robust minimax) type-I/II error over the uncertainty set
categories.robustness_nuisance: YES -- the entire problem is defined by the nuisance uncertainty/contamination set; D2T has no such set
categories.certificate_capability: LFD / robust-minimax characterisation; no interval-arithmetic certificate machinery
categories.computational_guarantee: Some tractable convex reformulations (Wasserstein); generally harder than D2T's exact finite enumeration
categories.reduction_reasoning: Different optimisation problem: D2T assumes fully-specified categorical laws (no nuisance/contamination set) and optimises a multi-action cost-constrained allocation; robust discrimination instead minimaxes over distributional uncertainty sets with a passive stream. The robustness_nuisance axis is structurally absent from D2T.
categories.d2t_capability_gap: D2T would need an explicit nuisance/uncertainty set to be comparable; adding one is out of the current scope and would change the problem.

key_references: Lindley 1956 (Bayesian experimental design / information gain)
DeGroot 1962 (uncertainty, information and sequential experiments)
Bernardo / Bayesian OED (EIG maximisation)
categories.hypothesis_space: Simple/composite hypotheses with a Bayesian prior; decision-region (acceptance) geometry under uncertainty
categories.action_control_space: Finite set of experiments; allocation chosen to maximise expected information gain
categories.fixed_sequential: Both fixed-sample and sequential OED variants
categories.adaptive_nonadaptive: Adaptive in sequential OED; open-loop in non-adaptive OED
categories.loss_endpoint: Expected information gain (EIG) / expected posterior uncertainty -- an INFORMATION objective, not a risk/error objective
categories.certificate_capability: No exact finite-budget risk certificate; EIG is typically estimated (MC / bounds)
categories.computational_guarantee: EIG estimation is expensive; no exact rational solution for the D2T risk endpoint
categories.reduction_reasoning: The repo runs an `eig` comparator (Hellinger-information greedy allocator, evaluation/matrix.py), i.e. Bayesian-EIG-style allocation on the SAME task / cost / horizon / endpoint. It is a registered comparator (coverage 4/64, family_cluster_mean_cost 8.0) in the frozen decision registry, though its objective (information) differs from D2T's (risk).
categories.d2t_capability_gap: Runs the same task as a comparator, but maximises information rather than certified risk; D2T's exact cost-to-endpoint with certificate is the residual capability.

categories.category_name: Test Cover (minimum test set for exact identification)
key_references: Moret & Shapiro 1985/1991, 'On Minimizing a Set of Tests', SIAM J. Sci. Stat. Comput. (test cover theory; greedy heuristics)
Crowston, Gutin et al. 2012 (parameterized complexity of Test Cover; O(log n) approx via Set Cover)
Garey & Johnson (NP-hardness)
categories.hypothesis_space: Finite set of items/candidates to identify uniquely; binary separability between every pair
categories.action_control_space: Finite set of binary tests; choose a minimum-cost subcollection that separates every pair (a test cover)
categories.observation_model: Binary test outcomes (which side of the test each item falls on); deterministic separation, no probabilities
categories.adaptive_nonadaptive: Non-adaptive (open-loop selection of a covering set)
categories.budget_cost: Cost of the chosen tests; minimise total cost of the cover
categories.loss_endpoint: Exact unique identification (zero discrimination error) via a covering set; NOT a probabilistic risk endpoint
categories.certificate_capability: NP-hard; approximation ratio O(log n) vs optimal; no risk certificate
categories.computational_guarantee: NP-hard, O(log n)-approx greedy; no exact polynomial algorithm
categories.rna_action_realism: Deterministic test separation only; no probabilistic RNA observation model
categories.reduction_reasoning: The repo runs a `greedy_test_cover` comparator (TV-separation greedy allocator, evaluation/matrix.py) on the SAME task/cost/horizon/endpoint; it is a registered comparator (coverage 0/64, family_cluster_mean_cost 8.0) in the frozen decision registry. Test Cover is genuine closest prior art for the action-selection combinatorial core.
categories.d2t_capability_gap: Test Cover is a deterministic binary covering problem (exact identification, no probabilities, no risk endpoint). D2T replaces this with probabilistic multi-action allocation under a randomised-minimax risk endpoint and a cost budget, with exact rational certificates -- a nontrivial extension beyond binary covering.

categories.category_name: RNA rational design (inverse folding / sequence design)
key_references: Inverse-folding / RNA design literature (e.g. NUPACK, RNAinverse, linearFold / Eterna-style design)
D2T-RNA is the motivating application of the D2T task
categories.hypothesis_space: RNA sequence space to be designed; objective is a target structure/function, not a statistical hypothesis
categories.action_control_space: Sequence / modification choices; no sensing-allocation control
categories.observation_model: Thermodynamic folding / structure-prediction models (minimum free energy), not categorical observation laws
categories.budget_cost: Design/optimisation cost, not measurement sampling cost
categories.loss_endpoint: Structural/functional fitness (e.g. MFE distance, expression level); no error-probability endpoint
categories.computational_guarantee: NP-hard / heuristic search (stochastic, dynamic programming); no exact guarantees
categories.rna_action_realism: Directly RNA; defines the DESIGN objective, not the discrimination action model
categories.reduction_reasoning: RNA rational design solves the sequence-design / inverse-folding problem (optimise a target structure), which is a DIFFERENT task from the D2T budgeted-hypothesis-test discrimination problem. RNA is only the motivating application domain of D2T; the design methods are not solution methods for the D2T decision problem.
categories.d2t_capability_gap: Not a comparator; relevant only as application framing for the D2T action model (see categories #8, #9).

categories.category_name: M2 / M2R / M2-seq mutational-profiling action realism
key_references: M2-seq style mutational profiling / MA (mutagenesis) action realism for the D2T action model (repo: data/measured_mattr.py, rna.py)
categories.hypothesis_space: D2T two-hypothesis discrimination (H0/H1 over sequence states); the actions are mutational-profiling experiments
categories.action_control_space: Realistic mutational-profiling actions (what a measurement actually observes); informs rna_action_realism of D2T
categories.budget_cost: Measurement cost of running a mutational-profiling assay
categories.loss_endpoint: None of its own -- it is a realism/specification input, not a loss-endpoint method
categories.rna_action_realism: HIGH -- this is precisely the action-realism axis
categories.reduction_reasoning: M2/M2R/M2-seq are experimental mutational-profiling protocols that specify the REALISM of the D2T action model (the channel a measurement induces); they are not competing solution algorithms for the D2T decision problem and carry no loss endpoint of their own.
categories.d2t_capability_gap: Feeds the rna_action_realism field of the D2T action model; not a comparator.

DMS-MaPseq (mutational profiling with next-gen reads) count model / calibration

categories.action_control_space: None (a single probing assay); informs the D2T observation model
categories.observation_model: Count-likelihood / calibration of probing read counts to structural state

categories.d2t_capability_gap: Feeds the observation_model field of D2T; not a comparator.
